paragraphs: In [Avodah Zarah 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.75a.11), the question is “How much is an onah?” Rav Chana She’onah, or according to another reading Rav Chana bar She’onah, cites Rabbah bar bar Chana in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. In [Niddah 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.65b.5) the reading is “Rav Chana She’onah, and some say Rav Chana bar She’onah.” Hyman reads [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1383&lang=en) as identifying him with Rabbi Yochanan bar She’onah, mentioned in Vayikra Rabbah 5:2.

notes.text: The consulted Avodah Zarah text gives Rabbi Chana Sheina or Rabbi Chana bar Sheina. The supplied notice has the Shaonah spelling and uses Rav in the quoted chain.

The parallel in [Niddah 65b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.65b.5) uses the She’ona spelling and calls him Rabbi in the consulted text. Heilprin groups these names and questions the claim of direct discipleship, pointing out the intermediate link through Rabbah bar bar Chana.
